summary: The endpoint demand bound is valid because a positive-difference label's lower endpoint has q_y<1, so its total lower-oriented demand is at most w_y-beta_y^b, which is bounded by the sum of the deletion and unsaturated-completion edge-end slacks incident to y. Independent finite bin allocations at each physical endpoint therefore give the claimed exact decomposition and per-edge-end capacity bounds; summing over the two distinct endpoints of each edge yields exactly the factor-two bounds. Complementary saturation for the fresh KKT pair implies every edge with b_e-omega_e^b>0 is hit by the single affine optimizer s_b, so its total slack is at most R_C(b), and the predecessor bounds then give all stated retainable-capacity inequalities. The algebra, strict inequalities, thresholds, constants, and the stated nonfinal scope all check, including the alternative at 3Q/1600.
